exceptions.reason: Published 2026-10-05: the unsafe-operation guard does not block git trailer command configuration. simple-git 3.36.0 is installed and the fix is in the 4.x line only. It is installed only beneath @wordpress/env (a devDependency), which uses it in two places: lib/download-sources.js, to clone and update the git sources named in a wp-env configuration, and lib/runtime/docker/download-wp-phpunit.js, to clone the WordPress test suite from a GitHub address written in that file. @wordpress/env 11.16.0, the latest release, requires simple-git ^3.32.3 and calls the package as a function (`require( 'simple-git' )( … )`). simple-git 4, where the fixes are, exports an object with a named `simpleGit` instead, so overriding it does not install a fix, it breaks `wp-env start`: the override was tried on 2026-10-07 and wp-env's own call sequence failed at the first line with "SimpleGit is not a function".
exceptions.control: The defect is a way round simple-git's refusal of dangerous git options, so it matters where somebody else chooses the arguments, the configuration or the environment simple-git is given. Here they come from one place: wp-env.json in this repository, which names a single git source, `WordPress/WordPress#master`, and the fixed option objects in wp-env's source. A person who can change that file can already run any command on the same machine through wp-env's documented `lifecycleScripts`, so the advisory gives them nothing they lack. It runs only when a developer starts wp-env (`npm run env:start`); no workflow under .github/ uses wp-env, and scripts/build-shared-host-dist.mjs ships plugin and theme source and never node_modules, so it reaches neither CI nor a WordPress site.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when @wordpress/env publishes a release that depends on simple-git 4.0.1 or later; a lockfile update then takes it with no override. Re-argue instead of renewing if wp-env.json gains a source whose URL or ref is not written in this repository, or if a CI workflow starts using wp-env: either would end the reasoning above.
